passage: I still remember the exact second it left my mouth. We were on the school bus, everyone was guessing who liked whom, and I was so excited to have real news that I said, "Parul is nervous about the singing audition. She might not go." She had told me not to tell anyone. Within an hour half of class ten knew. Next day Parul walked past me with her jaw set. At lunch I hid behind my book and rehearsed excuses: everyone already knew, you should have said it was serious. None of them sounded true. At the gate I caught her and said, "I told them. It was my fault. I was excited and I didn't think. I'm sorry." She said she was angry and didn't want to talk yet. I said okay and let her go. It stung, but it was fair. — Vasudha

qa.q: Where were Vasudha and the others when Vasudha said Parul's secret?
qa.a: They were on the school bus.

qa.q: Why did Vasudha stop rehearsing excuses?
qa.a: Vasudha was ashamed and could not face Parul, and none of the excuses sounded true, so Vasudha chose a plain apology instead.

qa.q: What made Vasudha's apology a wise one?
qa.a: Vasudha said "It was my fault" with no excuse, accepted that Parul was angry, and let her have distance.

qa.q: How might Parul have felt at the gate?
qa.a: Angry and hurt. Her jaw set earlier and her words that she did not want to talk yet suggest she needs space, and it may take time.

grounding: Vasudha leaked a friend's secret from excitement, cannot face her, and apologises plainly and gives distance.
